kubectl wait: "waits until the specified condition is seen in the Status field of every given resource." --timeout: "The length of time to wait before giving up." Deployment: "`type: Available` with `status: "True"` means that your Deployment has minimum availability. Minimum availability is dictated by the parameters specified in the deployment strategy." Run: `kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/rv-db --timeout=180s` -> `deployment.apps/rv-db condition met`.

"`Never`: Does not automatically restart the terminated container." Phases: "`Succeeded` | All containers in the Pod have terminated in success, and will not be restarted." "`Failed` | All containers in the Pod have terminated, and at least one container has terminated in failure. That is, the container either exited with non-zero status or was terminated by the system, and is not set for automatic restarting."

stage-2:scripts/k8s/deploy.sh 50-56: `if [ "$phase" != Succeeded ]; then kubectl logs pod/migrate -n donhang >&2 || true; exit 1; fi` then `echo "== the api"`, `kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s/api.yaml -o name`. On failure the script exits before api.yaml is applied, so the existing Deployment api is not changed and no rollout starts; its running Pods are untouched. Section 6 sentence and q2 explanations a/b match this; the bundle fact in b is established in devops.l2.migrations-in-the-pipeline.

issues.quote: `kubectl run --rm -i --restart=Never` starts a one-off Pod from the Caddy image, used here only because it contains `wget`, prints what it writes, and deletes it afterwards.
issues.text: The inserted clause 'used here only because it contains wget' sits between 'starts' and 'prints ... deletes', so on first read I took 'prints what it writes' as part of the Caddy clause. I had to re-read to see the three verbs belong to kubectl run.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: '`kubectl run --rm -i --restart=Never` starts a one-off Pod, prints what it writes, and deletes it afterwards. It uses the Caddy image only because that image contains `wget`.'
